commitResults.messageTitle: Add Java and Git conventions in AGENTS
Add commit and tag conventions in AGENTS

commitResults.messageBody: Read commands until bye, echo non-exit commands, and print a response separator after each command.
Give SlotBot the requested time-management greeting and friendly ending.
Start directly with the text-block greeting and keep the README output example in sync.
Explain the main command loop, exit behavior, and command echoing while removing unused imports.
Store non-command input in memory and display tasks with the list command so SlotBot supports the Level-2 add and list features.
Represent task descriptions and completion state so Level 3 commands can mark tasks done or not done.
Add a reusable workflow for generating self-contained GitHub-style HTML split-view diffs of repository changes.

Introduce Todo, Deadline, and Event subclasses while keeping
shared completion behavior in Task.

Parse todo, deadline, and event commands into their
corresponding Task subclasses.

Show task counts after adding tasks and use the required
list heading for todos, deadlines, and events.
Replace scattered multi-line printing with Java text blocks for
clearer output formatting.

Add input and expected-output regression testing.
Works for the Level-4 command-line interface.

Add SlotBotException-based validation for blank todo descriptions,
unknown commands, and malformed deadline/event input.
Show command-specific usage hints so users can correct errors without
changing the task list.

Extend the UI regression scenario with invalid inputs and document
the parser behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Document classes and methods with Javadocs
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace inline comments with Javadoc comments and add tags for
parameters, return values, and exceptions.
Keep short explanatory comments.

Record the Javadoc style in AGENTS.md for future changes.

Support delete NUMBER by removing the selected task from the task
collection and displaying the removed task with the updated count.

Extend UI regression coverage to verify deleting task 2 renumbers the
remaining tasks.

Use SlotBotException to report missing, non-numeric, and out-of-range
delete arguments with command-specific usage hints.

Show task-number placeholders as [NUMBER] and extend regression coverage
for invalid delete commands.

Add a common SlotBotException-based helper for mark, unmark, and
delete commands. Use command-specific [NUMBER] guidance for missing,
invalid, and out-of-range task numbers.

Extend UI regression coverage for all three commands.

Add CommandType to represent SlotBot's fixed command set and use it for
command routing and task parsing.

Keep task inheritance unchanged because Todo, Deadline, and Event already
represent their types through polymorphism.

commitResults.messageTitle: Isolate UI tests from runtime data
Add tests for invalid date handling

commitResults.messageBody:
Move command-type, task-number, and task creation parsing out of
SlotBot so parsing has one focused responsibility.

Keep command dispatch in SlotBot to preserve behavior and avoid
introducing command classes prematurely.

Replace direct collection management in SlotBot with a TaskList that
owns task addition, deletion, lookup, and counting.

Expose a read-only snapshot for persistence so external code cannot
change the collection directly.

Move command input and all user-facing output from SlotBot into Ui so
the main class can focus on coordinating application behavior.

Keep storage decisions in SlotBot while routing persistence warnings
through Ui to preserve existing messages.

Move file access, task serialization, and saved-task parsing out of
SlotBot so persistence has one focused owner.

Keep warning display delegated to Ui to preserve recovery behavior for
unreadable files and malformed records.

Move application classes into the slotbot package and group task
classes under slotbot.task to clarify their responsibilities.

Update the UI test runner to compile nested source files and launch the
packaged main class while preserving existing behavior.

Cover task-number parsing boundaries and invalid inputs.

Verify storage loading, task reconstruction, and malformed-record
recovery using isolated temporary files.

Rename the Shadow JAR output from duke.jar to slotbot.jar so the
generated distributable matches the application name.

Several Java declarations and switch blocks do not follow the required
SE-EDU naming, layout, and Javadoc conventions.

Apply the audited corrections while preserving application behavior, and
update the storage tests for the renamed boolean query.
Search task descriptions and display matching tasks in order.

Add the SE-EDU AddressBook rules and pin Checkstyle to 11.0.0 so
production and test code can be checked consistently with Gradle.
Treat warnings as failures and document the commands and reports.

The first run passes production sources and identifies 18 existing
test formatting violations to address in the next focused commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix Checkstyle violations in unit tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Move static assertions before other imports and keep lambda opening
parentheses on the preceding line to satisfy the SE-EDU rules.

Preserve all test scenarios and assertions. Production code and
console behavior remain unchanged; all 23 JUnit tests and the text
UI regression suite pass.

Add an isolated fixture check to verify that the configured rules
accept compliant Java and detect whitespace errors and naming
warnings. Assert that normal source checks reject violations.

Generate fixtures only under build and document the test command
so the configuration can be checked without changing user code.

Integrate Checkstyle configuration, test formatting fixes, and rule
enforcement tests. Preserve the focused increment commits and an
explicit integration point in the project history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add shared command responses for the GUI
commitResults.messageBody:
Expose stateful command responses so the graphical and console
interfaces can use the same parsing, task operations, and messages.
Route formatted output and storage warnings through a destination
without changing the save format or console transcript.

Add focused tests for command sequences, invalid input, exit state,
and persistence warnings, plus the Level-10 manual test plan.

Add a resizable conversation window with Enter and Send submission,
wrapping messages, automatic scrolling, and a timed goodbye.
Connect the interface to the shared command responses so existing
commands and storage warnings remain available.

Follow the tutorial dependency setup and use a separate launcher
for packaged JAR execution. Keep the console entry point and its
regression runner available alongside the graphical interface.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add GUI tests and manual testing instructions
commitResults.messageBody:
Add an opt-in JavaFX interaction test for FXML wiring, submission,
blank input, focus, and exit handling. Keep desktop tests separate
from the normal core test task.

Document launch commands and ordered manual scenarios with expected
results. Use isolated test data so GUI checks preserve user tasks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix scrolling to the latest reply
commitResults.messageBody:
Scrolling before the viewport finishes layout can leave the final
lines of a new response below the visible area.

Complete the scene layout before setting the bottom scroll position.
Add an offscreen regression that fails with the previous behavior
and checks both submission methods, wrapping, and manual scrolling.
Update the manual checklist with the reported failure scenario.

Integrate the JavaFX chatbot, shared command responses, GUI tests,
and the verified autoscroll fix after manual testing passes.
Preserve the focused increment commits and console compatibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add varargs support for displaying lines
commitResults.messageBody:
Add a shared UI method that accepts any number of lines and appends
the system line separator to each. Use it for task rows and storage
warnings, including the existing two-line load warning.

Preserve response text and persistence behavior. Add focused tests
for zero, one, and multiple lines, blank lines, and warning text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add spacing between logical code sections
commitResults.messageBody:
Separate list headers, task rows, and footers, and distinguish GUI
setup, message construction, and test scenarios with blank lines.

Keep related statements together. Change only blank lines so the
review improves readability without altering behavior or test data.

Integrate varargs-based line output and its focused tests while
preserving response text and persistence behavior. Include the
reviewed spacing improvements as a separate commit in the history.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for task list indexes
commitResults.messageBody:
Task indexes enter TaskList only after callers validate them.

An out-of-range index therefore indicates a programming error rather than
invalid input that TaskList should recover from.

Add assertions to get and delete so violations of this internal contract fail
close to their source. Add boundary tests to keep the contract explicit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions for task list contents
commitResults.messageBody:
TaskList assumes its collection and every stored task are present. Allowing
a null value would cause a less informative failure later during task
handling.

Add assertions to the constructor and add method to document this invariant.
Keep empty task lists valid for first-time users and test both cases.

User input and stored records are validated before task construction. A blank
description reaching Task therefore indicates a programming error.

Add a constructor assertion that applies consistently to every task subtype.
Cover null, empty, whitespace-only, and valid descriptions.

SlotBot.processCommand mixes command routing with the detailed steps for
updating a task's completion status. This makes the main command flow harder
to scan and maintain.

Extract the mark and unmark workflow into a focused method. Keep routing in
processCommand while preserving parsing, persistence, and error behavior.

SlotBot.processCommand contains the complete deletion workflow alongside its
routing decisions. This obscures the high-level command flow and leaves
low-level error handling in the main method.

Extract deletion into a focused method that keeps its parsing, persistence,
UI response, and error handling together without changing behavior.

SlotBot.processCommand handles keyword parsing and search errors inside the
command-routing flow. This makes the routing method responsible for details
that belong to the find operation.

Extract the find workflow into a focused method. Preserve matching and error
behavior while making the main command path easier to read.

SlotBot.processCommand performs task parsing, insertion, persistence, and UI
reporting as its fallback path. These details distract from the method's
command-routing responsibility.

Extract task creation into a focused method while retaining the same fallback
and error behavior. Stop refactoring once the router contains only concise
decisions and handler calls.

TaskList.findMatchingTasks selects elements from the existing task list.
The loop is correct, but it needs a mutable result list and manual
accumulation for a filtering operation.

Use a stream because filter directly represents that selection without
modifying the source list. Stream.toList preserves encounter order and
returns an unmodifiable result, matching the existing method contract.
This change improves clarity and provides stream practice; it is not a
performance optimization.
A-Assertions: Add internal invariant checks
A-CodeQuality: Refactor command handlers
A-Streams: Add stream-based task filtering

Deadlines need a reusable way to identify which unfinished items deserve
attention during a short reminder window.

Add date-window filtering that excludes completed and non-deadline tasks,
keeps boundary dates, and returns reminders sorted by due date. Cover the
normal, boundary, and invalid-input cases with deterministic tests.

Users need a direct way to see unfinished deadlines that need attention
soon.

Add the reminders command with a seven-day window, date ordering, and a
clear empty-state message. Inject a clock into SlotBot so reminder behavior
can be tested against fixed dates without changing normal construction.

The reminders command changes the console surface and needs to be
discoverable and regression-tested.

Document the seven-day deadline window, add an empty-state UI scenario,
and update the expected transcript after reviewing the intentional output.
B-Reminders: Add deadline reminders

Task commands can contain ambiguous separators, unsafe storage
characters, or event ranges that do not represent a valid schedule.

Accept flexible separator whitespace and reject repeated separators,
unsafe descriptions, and non-increasing event times before adding a
task. Add focused parser and application tests for the rejected inputs.

Invalid time ranges can enter the task model through sources other than
user commands, including malformed saved data.

Require every event to end after it starts so the model preserves a
valid time range. Verify that malformed saved events are skipped while
later valid records continue to load.

The text UI regression suite does not cover the new command validation
behavior.

Document the expected behavior and add transcript cases for ambiguous
separators, unsafe descriptions, invalid event ranges, and flexible
separator spacing.

Integrate the completed A-MoreErrorHandling increment after its input
validation and persistence safeguards pass automated and manual
verification.

Command recognition and task parsing have important success and failure
paths that are only exercised indirectly.

Add focused coverage for every command type and valid task
construction. Cover missing arguments, malformed dates, repeated
separators, and unsupported commands.

Task models and persistence contain boundary, formatting, and error
paths that are not covered directly.

Add coverage for status transitions, subtype rendering, and list
invariants. Cover serialization, malformed records, and filesystem
failures.

Several response formats and command-routing cases are not asserted
directly.

Cover console input and output formatting, storage warnings, exact
commands, duplicate tasks, and requests received after exit.

The JavaFX interaction tests combine setup, actions, and assertions in
long methods that are difficult to scan.

Add focused helpers for view setup, command submission, scrolling, and
exit checks. Preserve the existing scenarios while keeping each test
method at one abstraction level.

Narrowing the window can rewrap existing messages after the
conversation has already scrolled to its old bottom.

Keep the conversation pinned when a resize changes wrapped content.
Preserve a user's manual scroll position and add a GUI regression test
for both behaviors.

Task creation combines command dispatch, field validation, and date
conversion in one long method.

Add focused helpers for each task type and shared field validation.
Keep Parser responsible for constructing tasks while preserving
existing commands and error messages.

Integrate the completed testing increment after its expanded unit and
GUI coverage passes review. Include the related code-quality refactors
and regression checks.

Preserve the feature branch history with a non-fast-forward merge.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add feedback for empty find results
commitResults.messageBody:
Empty find results showed a heading without any task rows.

This made a completed search look unfinished.

Show the search keyword in an explicit response.

Conversation messages stretched across most of the window.

This made short replies resemble cards instead of chat bubbles.

Add sender-aligned rows with constrained, wrapping content.

Cover the new structure and responsive behavior in GUI tests.

The interface used a functional but visually flat presentation.

Improve visual hierarchy with a calm palette and clearer controls.

Use consistent spacing while preserving the existing layout.

Bot replies looked identical for successful and invalid commands.

Classifying errors from text would couple styling to wording.

Return immutable response metadata and use it to style errors.

Keep command processing and console output unchanged.

The optional GUI work is complete and verified on its feature branch.

Merge the reviewed history without flattening its logical commits.

The docs page contained placeholder sections and no product image.

Replace it with a concise guide covering every command and input rule.

Add a realistic full-window screenshot for the published website.

Impossible calendar values used the same wording as date-format errors.

Report invalid deadline and event values directly. Assert the messages in
parser and text-interface regressions.

Past dates and accepted whitespace can be surprising without guidance.

Document reminder treatment of overdue deadlines and the supported spacing
rules without presenting intentional behavior as a bug.

Invalid calendar values need clearer feedback before the final release.

Merge the reviewed parser, regression, and User Guide updates while
preserving their logical commits.

Unknown-command errors omit find, reminders, and delete, making it
harder for users to discover supported commands.

List every supported command in the fallback message and add
regression coverage to keep the guidance complete.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add stable numbering to find results
commitResults.messageBody:
Find results previously renumbered matches independently from the full
list. This could make mark, unmark, and delete target another task.

Preserve each match's original list number and document the shared
numbering. Add regression coverage for non-consecutive matches.
